Comments: On 5/9/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite, followup inspection for the Watson 1 well, API 129-24979. The separator and chart housing is surrounded by vegetation, it is recommended the operator remove the vegetation to better inspect the well. The operator information and tag was placed as seen in photographs 1 and 2. The wellhead and equipment displayed light to moderate corrosion. The production chart was labeled 11-29-2023 and showed constant production. During the time of the inspection the 2023 APR/MIA has not been received. All line valves were open as seen in photographs 7, 10, 11, and 12 and the well appeared to be producing. This appears to be an active producing well. OGI used a Bascom Turner EGA 411 to detect for the presence of gas. Gas was detected to be coming from the base of the wellhead at a peak of 12% gas as seen in photograph 8. No gas was detected in the surrounding soils or on the other equipment. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8160353
Permit API: 065-25518
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Knox Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/22/2023
Comments: This site located west off Odonnell Road, 1 1/2 miles south of railroad crossing on State Game Lands Road, at the end of second branch to the north. Well is set-up for production with a meter, separator and one tank. A report of a release of 32 gallons of produced water was reported by Will Warfel with Diversified Prod LLC at 12:30 on 9/21/23 at this well site. The release was assumed to be from the separator, there is an area of dead vegetation around the well head, separator and meter and a path 70x15' path to the west. Contaminated soil needs to be removed from site and hauled to a licensed disposal facility. Clean-up on this site not started at the time of this inspection. There was no discussion about visual or Act 2 clean-up at this site, however it appears that that the release was more than a barrel and Act 2 remediation is requested. WQS Taylor met Paul Stiner on his way to this site with an excavator and dump truck to begin clean-up of this well site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-07-11 to Xto Energy Inc in Chapman Twp, Clinton county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Xto Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-07-11
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 855600
Permit API: 035-21316
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-11
Comments: I met with Shawn Gearhart of XTO when I arrived. Containment was being pulled up on the side of the pad closest to the entrance. I noted two distinct areas of stressed vegetation off the west side of the pad (see map), and soil conductance readings were elevated off the entire west side of the pad. Where the containment had been removed, I was able to get conductance readings in several puddles. Near where the blender had been during the frac, I found two puddles with elevated conductance (5.31 and 7.49 mS/cm, see map for location). Puddles on the north side of the pad showed low conductance (.79-1.2 mS/cm). No XTO EH&S representative was present on the site during my inspection. Outstanding violations from 7/5/19 inspection cited.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up Inspection (FUI) of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K Well Site located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/5/22 @1045 hours. The weather was 70 degrees, light rain, winds S @5mph. Seneca Company Man, Travis Deleon was present onsite.During the previous inspection (IR#3376280) dated 6/10/22, a damp area and puddle was observed below the hose connection to the Highland production tank. The puddle had a field measured conductivity of 11.02 mS/cm. Sample 4427-261 was collected from the standing fluid and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for analysis. The sample results show the presence of a pollutional substance. Barium was reported at 44.78 mg/L, strontium was reported at 166.9 mg/L, and chlorides were present at 3410.8 mg/L. As of today's inspection, a small piece of secondary containment was observed installed under the hose connection on the rear side of the Highland storage tank. The area under the secondary containment was observed damp with a small amount of standing fluid. A Groline soil conductivity meter was used to measure the field conductivity of the damp soils from 1.97mS/cm - 2.37 mS/cm. A comparison of the previous photo taken of the area during the inspection on 6/10/22, to the current state of the area, indicates no pad material was removed from the impacted area. I spoke with a Seneca representative onsite and he stated production would be dispatching someone to the site to remediate the area today. A vac truck arrived onsite and removed the remaining production fluids from the Highland tank and drained the secondary containment. I again spoke with an onsite well tender regarding the removal of impacted pad material. He spoke with Jim Westbrook and stated Gas Field Specialists had been dispatched to the site and would arrive this afternoon. I completed my inspection and departed the site at 1300 hours. Gas Field Specialist personnel located me while conducting an inspection at the nearby Pad D. I informed them of the area with elevated conductivity on Pad K, where they were headed, and we discussed removal of the impacted pad material. They requested I return to the site after they had removed the impacted material to screen the area with a soil conductivity meter. None of the GFS personnel or onsite Seneca representatives possessed a conductivity meter. The impacted pad material was removed with shovels and 5 gallon buckets and placed on temporary secondary containment. I screened the excavated area for soil conductivity and found readings of less than 800 uS/cm. The area was backfilled with clean material and the secondary containment was repositioned under the hose connection. GFS personnel said they would provide the cleanup information and pictures to Seneca for followup with the DEP.Violations of the following regulations remain outstanding against API#117-22143 165HU awaiting the information requested in the NOV issued in IR#3387022 :CLS 402(b)SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a57 control, storage and disposal of production fluids25 Pa Code 78a66(b)I again departed the site at 1530 hours.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of a routine inspection. The well is currently awaiting a service rig, per the operator, and has not been recently pumped. It appears as though a leak occurred on this site sometime in the past year, and it was covered with absorbent peat and then left. The spill was not reported to DEP. The quantity of oil spilled is unknown, but appears to be greater than 5 gallons and less than one barrel. Oil stained soil with absorbent peat is noted in an L shape approximately 10 feet wide and 30 feet long that extends to the edge of the location. Absorbent peat is noted closer to the edge of the site, primarily. A small UNT of Briggs Run begins at the edge of the site. One oil soaked pad was noted in this ditch lone, although no oil was noted in the ditch at this time. The operator was contacted and they arrived on site to begin assessment and cleanup on 8/25. Per the operator, the spill occurred over this past winter and the well pumper covered the spill with peat sorb, which then settled as it was not cleaned up as the winter went on. Spring melt allowed the material to run to the edge of the site. Per the operator, the employee is no longer with the company. Cleanup should be completed in the next few days. Followup inspection will be performed at that time.The operator was also asked about the steep and rutted access roads on this lease and said that they have recently acquired a new bulldozer and intend to grade and fix lease roads soon.

Comments: On 03/04/2025 representatives from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently completed wells onsite and their American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers are posted at the site entrance; I was unable to confirm if the wells were tagged due to them currently being covered (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which did not contain any standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure did not contain any standing water. The tanks were labeled as per the Department's request (photos #5 and 6). A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and held in secondary containment (photo #7).Numerous upright brine tanks and temporary storage tanks are still noted onsite and held in their respective secondary containment structures which appear to be functioning as intended (photos #8 and 9). Multiple lined and covered residual waste containers are in use onsite for ongoing Act 2 remediation efforts as well as disassembly of the pad wide containment system (rig matting) and tear down of completions equipment (photos #10 and 11). The modular aboveground storage structures (MASS) have been removed and the brine offload area has been disassembled (photo #12).Remediation remains ongoing from the releases on 12/04/2024 and 12/09/2024 (Inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285) as the areas formerly covered by rig matting and containment structures are now accessible. Pad drainage systems remain shut in to prevent any water from ice and snow melt from leaving the pad. I did not observe any diesel sheen on the pad surface. Water is being removed from the well pad via an onsite vacuum truck as it accumulates. The area located underneath the brine offload area from the release on 12/09/2024 is currently being excavated to comply with Act 2 remediation standards (photo #13). Soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity at ~1.68mS/cm and fluids accumulating in this area field measured for EC at ~15.67mS/cm (photos #14 and 15). These soils and fluids are being collected via vacuum truck or lined residual waste container.Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed at the time of this inspection due to snow coverage. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review in the mailbox at the site entrance (photo #16). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #17). The basin inlet remains shut in and no fluids or diesel sheen was observed (photo #18). Soil in the basin field measured for EC at ~0.72mS/cm (photo #19).Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: Today inspection report is an Administrative report from OGI Eric Miller, who was unable to be on site at the conclusion of the shut in tests. OGI Dave Schoonover was on location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build-Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on both wells on the DeWolf pad, the Evelyn Wyo. 4H and the Evelyn Wyo. 2H. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps. (Dakota Manning and Ryan Carmody), using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. 8/3/23) Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. Violation ID: 8256800
Permit API: 125-28998
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Buffalo Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/19/2025
Comments: On November 19, 2025, the Department conducted a Partial Routine inspection on the access road of the Breese well site in Buffalo Township, Washington County. The site Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) was terminated by the Department on July 10, 2020. During this inspection, the Department observed torn Compost Filter Sock (CFS) installed in the roadside ditch of the access road entrance. This torn CFS was overtopped by sediment which accumulated in the roadside channel (photos 2 and 3). No sediment was observed in the stormwater culvert where the roadside ditch empties (photos 3 and 4). The ground was scoured by stormwater on eastern side of the access road (photo 5). The Department followed this scouring up the access road to a deep accelerated erosion rill adjacent to the well pad (photo 6). This deep accelerated erosion rill appears to be the source of the scouring and sedimentation shown in Photos in 2-5, due to the potential for channelized stormwater flow.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued against the overtopped CFS and the accelerated erosion and sedimentation in the access road.

Comments: On August 7, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Monona's Stickle 1H (129-28411) well located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4011517 where violations were issued for an out of compliance Act 9 Sign and an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP) Accompanying during today's inspection is Monona Operator Tom Stickle and Plants and Goodwin's Representative Jim Watson.Documented in IR 4029415, the Department received a Notice of Violation (NOV) Operator Response from Mr. Stickle on 7/28/25 which stated that all violations should be corrected by August 31, 2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance, the Department recommends the Operator replace the Act 9 Sign with one that satisfies 78a55(i)4ii. In the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan (ERP), however it had adifferent Operator's name posted on it, the Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site perimeters appeared to be exhibiting at last 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Stickle stated that they are actively working on a new Act 9 sign and an updated ERP and would notify the Department of its completion and installation on site. At the time of this inspection, the Stickle 1H well site appeared to have 2 wells on it, the 1H (129-28411) had a well tag fixed to the wellhead with the well's name and permit number posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of the production equipment observed on site at this time.During IR 4011517, the Department observed a plethora of production equipment not in use scattered around the well site and within the production tank's secondary containment. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed most of the production equipment that was previously scattered about the well site to be removed at this time. Mr. Stickle stated that the remaining equipment observed on the ground and within the secondary containment would be removed from the well site within the next few weeks. During IR 4011517, the Department observed corrosion holes in the production tanks on site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed these holes to be freshly patched. Mr. Stickle stated both tanks will be painted in the coming weeks to prevent any further corrosion. Violations issued against the 129-28648 well which is located on the same well pad as the 129-28411 for a release(s) of an oily substance related to the reported replugged of the well is being assessed under a separate inspection for 129-28648.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an Act 9 sign not in compliance and an outdated ERP shall remain outstanding at this time and violations issued for corrosion holes in the production tank shall be closed at this time.

Inspection Date: 6/04/2024
Comments: This site located in a grassy field west off Parks Road at the end of a short access, 320' west of residence and the spring used for their water supply. Well set-up for production with a separator, drip and 100 barrel tank in secondary containment. Annual electronic production report submitted through 2023. Will Warful reported on 5/9/2024 that the nipple on the holding tank rotted and leaked the contents of the 100 barrel holding tank into the unlined secondary containment. A vac truck was used to remove the water that remained in the secondary containment. At this inspection more contaminated material was removed from area where the tank was located in secondary containment, part of secondary containment embankment and ~50' northwest of the original release area. Water in the hole excavated northwest of the secondary containment was tested with handheld conductivity meter, the reading was over 4 milli Siemens. Water pooled in the hole where the secondary containment was excavated was ~2 milli siemens. You are hereby requested to continue to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in afternoon with cold, partly sunny weather conditions, and 40 degrees. Last inspection performed on 3/29/17, more than 5 years ago. Wellhead is located in soybean Agriculture field planted/harvested ~1,750' SE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is not in close and barely visible proximity to the production facility with another well on property and shared facility. At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, right side production tubular valve closed to port, production tubular left side valve is closed, and the production tubular plumbed on left side of head to sales/surface equipment with closed valve; annulus is exposed and vented to the atmosphere with plumbed tubular sticking out of ground and open valve union (photo #2). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is not in close, barely visible proximity to the production facility and does require a well label/marker. Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well labeling OGA3211(H). The Department is requesting Operator add permanent well label/marker affixed at or to wellhead capturing the well details. The shared, multiple, two well (085-24005 and 085-23892) surface/ground production facility, two 50 bbl poly tanks, and two 100 bbl steel tanks all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #3). The subject well of this inspection contains surface/ground production equipment, one 50 bbl poly tank and one 100 bbl steel tank (photo #4). Valve closed on main tubular feeding separator and closed valves to and from separator (photo #5). Copper tubing lines are disconnected from production recording apparatus/chart cabinet (photos #6). A 31-day production chart is present, but not attached and without recordings dated 6/1/22 (photo #7). No production is being recorded. Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #8). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021, 2020, and 2019 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2018 of 91 Mcf recorded over 90 days. Wellhead field verified and GPS coordinates of well updated with this inspection showed a moderate distance offset of ~46 ft between coordinates (photo #9). This well is shut in at the wellhead and at the surface/ground production facility and continues to be temporarily not producing.

Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Comments: On August 22, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022.Precision Drilling Rig 110 is onsite and in the process of drilling the 1003H lateral. Precision Drilling has already drilled the 1005H well and have one more well lateral to complete. There were 8 oil based mud tanks, 4 cement tanks, 5 frac tanks and 4 floc water tanks in secondary containment. The containment around the drill rig was in good condition. A vacuum truck is onsite to vacuum up the water in the secondary containment. STL Resources was in the process of pumping out the northwest stormwater vault on the well pad from recent rainfall. The water from the northwest stormwater vault was being pumped into 5 frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter. The water in the southwest stormwater vault was about 6 feet from the top of the vault. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 2 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 33.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 76.1 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers.Three monitoring wells have been drilled about 50 yards to the west of the well pad. All the infiltration berms at the site have been hydro seeded. The percent vegetated cover varies from berm to berm. The recently rebuilt northwest and southwest infiltration berms at the well pad are beginning to become vegetated. The water in the northwest infiltration berm was screened for conductivity and resulted in 230 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/18/2025
Comments: I was informed by my supervisor that Bull Run Resources had reported a release at their Backwards L #3 well located in Hamilton Township, McKean County. A gathering line failed and an unknown amount of crude oil was released. The release traveled down a road ditch approximately 500 feet heading in a southwest direction to a culvert crossing. The release continued through the culvert heading north for close to 190 feet, before stopping in what is best described as an infiltration sump for the ditch line. The sump contained the release and prevented it from reaching Chappel Fork. JR from Bull Run was onsite with a mini excavator and a lined dumpster that was being filling with impacted soil. He is continuing to work his way down the ditch line removing impacted soil and debris. The sump will be cleared of leaves and debris before being pumped out. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility. Future inspections will be performed to document the ongoing cleanup. Confirmatory sampling of the remediated area is expected to be conducted when remediation is complete. Documentation regarding the disposal of the contaminated soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.Please acknowledge receipt of this inspection and attached violations by emailing me at ebruce@pa.gov.

Permit API: 125-23126
Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 11/15/2023
Comments: On 11/15/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Cowden 55 well. On 08/23/2023, a routine partial inspection was conducted (IR 3606258).On 08/23/2023, the tank onsite displayed oil which looked as thought it was dripping down the side fro the top. The oil was on a small section of gravel. A smaller section of oil was on another side of the tank. The operator was notified the day of observation. There were no violations issued on 08/23/2023 due to size of area impacted. During inspection on 11/15/2023, for following was observed: The site appeared remediated regarding the oil from the top of the tank; the operator removed the impacted gravel and placed it in a bucket marked with 08/24/2023. The bucket remianed onsite; I recommend that this is removed and disposed of a an approproate waste facility (Photos 1-4). It also looked as thought the operator had wiped the side of the tank off. During the followup, a conductivity test was performed underneath the lower valve on the tank, which displayed iron stained gravel. Conductivity readings within the iron stained gravel, under the valve, yielded elevated results (Photos 5-7).During the initial inspection, a gas odor was noticed near the wellhead and I informed the operator. They informed operation's to inspect. They informed me that the grey apparatus on the well (Photo 8) was part of the landowner's hookup. When the operator followed up, their gas meter did not detect any gas. During the 11/15/23 follow up, the odor was noticed again to which I informed the operator. They followed up the same day and mentioned that the heater on the landowner's setup was functioning properly and may be bleeding; they recommendded a pressure test be performed. I contacted the landowner to inform them of what Diversified (operator) informed me of - they also contacted the landowner. I contacted the landowner about my conversation with the operator and recommended that the setup receives maintenance. The operator informed me that they thought the odor contained mercaptan and may be coming from a Columbia gas line nearby. Below the wellsite is a Williams station that the gas flows to. Regarding the elevated conductivity observed onsite below the valve of the production tank, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b)

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Haralambous G 03-074 well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 4/24/2023 at 1015 hours. The weather was 45 degrees with mostly cloudy skies. An Act 9 sign remains at the entrance to the well site.I met with the Repsol representative who reported to the DEP that on Friday, 4/21/2023, an unknown quantity of rainwater released off the edge of the pad surface from a tear in a secondary containment structure. Repsol also reported that Elk Environmental was dispatched to address the incident on 4/21/2023. Elk Environmental collected samples to determine the analytics of the stormwater. Pooled water off the edge of the pad surface was field measured at ~1200us/cm (photos # 2 and 3). Rainfall over the past two days has filled the secondary containment back up. Repsol reported that a water truck was scheduled to remove the additional rainwater from the containment today. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371607 is tied to this reported incident within CTS.The four recently hydraulically fractured wells onsite remain under flowback conditions at this time. One additional preexisting well remains capable of production. Numerous temporary storage containers are held within secondary containment onsite. Pooled water on the pad surface that was field measured for electrical conductivity ranged from 220 to 750us/cm today. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed. Violations cited against API #015-23745 on 12/20/2022 and 12/28/2022 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations are cited at this time. The DEP requests the analytical sample results from the samples collected related to the stormwater release. I departed the site at 1140 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8179679
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2024
Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-04-10 to Irvine Run Resources in Brokenstraw Twp, Warren county. CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Irvine Run Resources
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-04-10
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 847456
Permit API: 123-26419
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-04-10
Comments: This inspection was performed in response to the report of a small release of production fluid along Irvine Run, in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County, PA. Rick Engelbert, with Irvine Run Resources, contacted the Department to report a broken pipeline which resulted in the release of approximately ½ of a barrel of crude oil, to the ground along Irvine Run. The spill was reported to have been contained and was actively being cleaned up. The spill was reported to have been discovered at 14:30, on April 8, 2019. The spill was immediately responded upon by the operator. Legree 30, (37-123-26419): Upon receiving notification of this incident, I contacted Rick to arrange a site visit. I arrived on site at approximately 13:00 on April 10, 2019 to conduct a site investigation. The spill appeared to have occurred as previously described. Production fluid was released from a broken fitting on a buried gathering line. The spill allegedly occurred while the well was being pumped. Crude oil was noticed to have been seeping from the stream bank, approximately 40 feet below the damaged fitting. A small amount of fluid did travel down stream from the discharge point. Pumping was immediately stopped. Approximately 1.5 cubic yards of soil had been excavated around the damaged fitting. There did not appear to be any contaminated soil left in the hole. There did not appear to be all that much contaminated soil even in the material that had been excavated. The area on the stream bank where the fluid was noticed to have been emerging was just above the stream channel. There was no clearly exposed conduit or outlet, only an area of soil that was slightly saturated with crude oil. Small amounts of emulsified oil could be seen pooling in water as far as 80 feet down stream of the original discharge point. Much of the oil appeared to have been absorbed and/or contained by a series of absorbent pads and booms that the operator had placed along the channel. There did not appear to have been any oil at all pooling behind the final boom in the series, approximately 120 feet down-stream of the discharge point. I advised that the operator construct a small syphon dam directly in front of the initial point of discharge, and to continue changing pads and booms as needed. Clean-up progress will be monitored with future inspections.

Report Details

Violation Date: 9/19/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8159309
Permit API: 081-21855
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.

Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection (FUI) on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.On a FUI on 8/19/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3816085), I noted the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. I emailed Ray Hepler information about Act 2 remediation. On 8/28/2024, Jack Crow, Henry Kramer, Brian Shank and myself met with Ray Hepler at the PA DEP Meadville Regional Office to discuss the outstanding violations at the Wheeler property. Ray Hepler stated he had the contaminated soil from the brine releases on a roll off and would send us the manifests soon. The Department received a manifest for waste on 9/9/2024. However, the manifest stated the soil was "Beaver-PA 100%". The manifest also stated the soil was hauled in a "white pick up truck", but during the 8/28/2024 meeting Ray Hepler stated the soil was in a roll off container. This manifest does not show the proper disposal of the soil from the Wheeler W12 well site located in Jefferson County. Today (9/12/2024), Brian Shank and I conducted a FUI. The pipe not necessary for production was still being stored near the access road. The spill area appeared to have new top soil and grass seed. We collected soil conductivity readings throughout the spill area. A background soil conductivity reading was collected. The soil conductivity reading was 154.5 pS/cm. Near the production tank, the soil conductivity reading was 3.28 mS/cm. Approximately 4 feet from the production tank, the soil conductivity reading 1416 pS/cm. These readings indicate that the prior spill has not been remediated yet. We collected grab soil samples to send to the Department's accredited laboratory. The samples will be analyzed for SAC 960 and UVIR.The outstanding violations for the Wheeler W12 well site will remain open at this time.

Inspection Date: 2019-04-15
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted and INCIDENT inspection of the SWEPI LP - Kennedy 137 well pad located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 4/15/2019 @1000 hours the weather was 43 degrees, rain, winds W 18mph. Approximately 0.6 inches of precipitation was received over the past 24 hours. On 4/14/2019 @1700 hours, Shell representatives called in a spill of a reported 90 BBLs of production fluid to the pad surface of the Kennedy 137. A truck driver had discovered a hose connected to one of the Highland production tanks that was discharging production fluid to the pad surface. The driver assumed the Highland tank was at maximum capacity when it discharged it's contents. Mr. Bernethy, SWEPI Environmental Coordinator, contacted the WQS this morning to state the driver was mistaken. The Highland tank was not at capacity and the revised amount of the spill is 3-4 BBLs. Mr. Bernethy stated the spill was estimated to have impacted ~300-400 square feet of pad surface. As of yesterday evening, a vac truck had removed standing fluid from the pad surface,and a sump was constructed below the discharge valve from the Highland tank to remove accumulated fluid. Mr. Bernethy stated the sump will be regularly monitored and fluid removed as needed. As of today's inspection, no personnel were observed onsite. The impacted area below the Highland tank was observed flagged with cones and spray paint. The constructed sump was observed, and the fluid being held had a field measured conductivity of 1.00 mS/cm. All other puddles screened on the pad surface had a field measured conductivity of <1.0mS/cm. The fluid in the E&S channel below the fill slope was screened and found to be <1.0mS/cm. The E&S trap below the fill slope was also screened and found to be <1.0mS/cm. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time do to the reported release of 3-4 barrels of production fluid to the pad surface: CSL402b Potential Pollution SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.57 control, storage and disposal of production fluids. We departed the site @ 1100 hours.
